newsitem.title: USA: COLUMBIA/HCA PAYS LEGAL FEES OF THREE EXECS.
newsitem.headline: COLUMBIA/HCA PAYS LEGAL FEES OF THREE EXECS.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp said Wednesday it was paying the legal expenses of three company executives indicted on charges of defrauding the federal Medicare program.
The disclosure coincides with a Wall Street Journal report that federal prosecutors have declared Columbia itself a target of a criminal investigation of its business.

The Journal also said federal prosecutor Kathleen Haley had expressed concern that a conflict of interest could arise if the same defense attorneys represented the company and the indicted executives.
Asked if Columbia were paying the legal fees of the three mid-level executives indicted by a Florida federal grand jury two weeks ago, Columbia spokesman Jeff Prescott told Reuters, "Yes we are."
Prescott said it was "very standard practice" for companies to pay legal fees for employees who become targets of investigations.
"If things come up in the course of their employment it's very common (for an employer) to pay their attorneys' fees. We're certainly going to do that," he said.
